question.text: Which of the following is a consequence of underestimating retirement goals?

answer.text: Excess corpus available at the end of retirement
The retiree may need to scale back their lifestyle or postpone retirement
Higher returns on the retirement corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook (pages 28-29), underfunding a retirement plan can require postponing retirement or choosing a less expensive lifestyle, which directly matches option B. The Trap: Option A inverts the outcome (underestimation causes shortfall, not excess); options C and D describe favourable conditions (higher returns, lower inflation), neither of which is a consequence of underestimating goals. Note: When goals are underestimated, the corrective levers are limited to lifestyle, retirement age, or supplementary income - hence the workbook's emphasis on careful goal estimation up-front.
